description: Which slow TFs detect end-of-move (bear cross = exit signal). Core question: does D alone catch tops or do we need 4h confirmation?
How many lead TFs must turn bearish before exit process starts. 1=early exit (less drawdown) vs 3=ride longer (more profit but bigger pullbacks)
Use WT cross (wt1 crosses below wt2) vs velocity for lead exit signal. Cross is discrete event; velocity is continuous
4h WT velocity threshold to signal exhaustion. Less negative = earlier exit. More negative = only exit on strong reversals
Daily WT velocity threshold. D moves slowly so thresholds should be less negative than LTF
WT extreme zone threshold on lead TFs. When WT > this on 4h/D position is extended and more likely to reverse
WT percentile on 4h/D above which we consider the move extended. 90th percentile = historically extreme
Which momentum state on lead TFs triggers exit. EXHAUST_UP = momentum fading. IMPULSE_DOWN = already reversing
Require wave phase CONTRACTING on lead TF before exit. Contracting = WT1/WT2 converging = momentum dying
Use WT divergence (BEAR or HIDDEN_BEAR on 4h/D) as exit lead signal. Bear div = price HH but WT LH = weakening
WT peak structure on lead TF that signals exit. LH (lower-high) = downtrend starting. LL = already in downtrend
Which fast TFs find the best exit price after lead signals end-of-move. 3m = most precise but noisiest
How many confirm TFs must agree. 1=fast exit on first LTF turn. 2=wait for confirmation (better price but risk of missing)
What signal on confirm TF triggers actual exit. BEAR_CROSS = discrete WT cross. any_bear = cross OR velocity
3m WT velocity for exit confirmation. 3m is noisy so too sensitive = whipsaws. Too loose = miss the top
15m WT velocity for exit confirmation. 15m is smoother than 3m so can be tighter
Max bars since bear cross on confirm TF to count as active. Old crosses are stale
If WT is rising since last bear cross on confirm TF should we still exit? Rising = bounce starting = maybe hold
Global WT velocity exit threshold (current live value). Core sensitivity knob for all exits
WT acceleration (rate of change of score). Negative acceleration = momentum decelerating even if still positive
WT score (wt1-wt2) below which exit triggers. 0 = exit when wt1 crosses below wt2. -10 = wait for deep cross
Minimum WT score on 3m for entry confirmation. Higher = stronger signal but fewer entries
Minimum WT score on 15m for entry confirmation. 15m is the primary entry TF
Max bars since bull cross on 3m to count entry as valid. Too old = momentum already spent
Max bars since bull cross on 15m. 15m bars are longer so allow more lookback
Minimum 3m WT velocity for entry. Ensures momentum is accelerating into entry
Minimum 15m WT velocity for entry. Lower than 3m because 15m moves slower
Required momentum state on 3m for entry. IMPULSE_UP = strong fresh move. any_bull = also allow EXHAUST_DOWN (reversal starting)
Require EXPANDING wave phase on 15m for entries. Expanding = WT diverging = new trend starting
Require WT extreme oversold on at least one TF before long entry. Catches bottoms but misses trend continuations
Max WT percentile on 3m for entry. If already at 90th percentile the move is extended and risky to enter
Give extra score for bullish divergence (price LL but WT HL) on entry TF. Hidden strength signal
Required WT trough structure on 15m for entries. HL (higher-low) = uptrend. LL = still falling
Which TF Donchian breakout to use for entries. 1h = current. 4h = fewer but stronger signals
Score added when price breaks DC high/low. Higher = must combine with other signals
Minimum % price must exceed DC channel boundary. Filters fake breakouts
Minimum DC width (% of price) for breakout to count. Narrow channels = chop. Wide = real volatility
Require DC channel to be expanding (widening) for breakout entry. Expansion = volatility increasing = trend starting
DC position below this for long entries (above 1-this for shorts). Lower = closer to channel bottom = better value
Which TF DC position to use for entry zone filter. 1h avoids noise. 4h = very slow filter
DC position above this signals long is near channel top (end of move). Exit lead signal from DC
Which TF DC position to check for exit. 1h = main. Adding 4h catches multi-day tops
Exit when DC width is contracting (channel narrowing). Narrowing after expansion = move exhausting
DC width must contract by this % from recent peak to trigger exit signal. 10% = moderate contraction
Exit long when price crosses below DC basis (midline). Losing the midline = trend weakening
Which TF DC basis crossunder to watch. 15m = responsive. 4h = confirms trend break
Exit long if price breaks below DC low (channel bottom). Strong reversal signal but very late
Use fast 4-bar DC crossunder for exit timing on confirm TFs. 4-bar DC reacts faster than standard
Which TF 4-bar DC to use for fast exit confirmation. 3m = most responsive for precise exit timing
Partial exit fraction at low gains (0.3-0.5%). Lower = keep more position. Higher = bank small profits faster
Partial exit fraction at medium gains (0.5-1.0%). Balance between taking profit and letting it run
Partial exit fraction at high gains (1-3%). Even at high gains cutting 75% might be too aggressive if trend continues
Minimum TFs with bullish WT for long entry. Higher = more confirmation but fewer entries
Minimum TFs with bearish WT for short entry. Same logic as bull alignment
Minimum wt_composite_delta (long-short difference) for entry. Ensures net directional bias across TFs
Require wt_composite_bias to match entry direction. False = allow entries against overall bias if LTF signals strong
Minimum oversold TF count for long entries. More oversold TFs = deeper pullback = better entry
How many TFs must be overbought to trigger exit lead. More = stricter = holds longer
If wt_hh_count (higher-high count across TFs) drops below this while in profit trigger exit consideration. Trend weakening
If wt_ll_count rises above this for a long position trigger exit. Multiple TFs making lower-lows = trend reversing
Scale position size by DC width (volatility). Wider channel = more volatile = maybe size down or up depending on trend
Maximum DC width sizing multiplier. Caps how much DC width can boost size
Scale size by DC position. At channel edge (trending) = larger size. At center (sideways) = smaller
Maximum multiplier at DC edges. 3x = current. 5x = very aggressive in trends
Minimum multiplier at DC center. Below 1.0 actively reduces size in sideways markets
DC lookback period for edge detection. Shorter = more reactive. Longer = smoother trend identification
Size multiplier based on WT composite delta strength. Strong alignment = bigger position
Scale size by number of aligned TFs. 5/5 bullish = full size. 2/5 = half size
WT exit velocity in ranging regime. Ranging = exits should be faster (smaller moves)
WT exit velocity in trending regime. Trending = exits should be slower (let winners run)
Reduce fraction in ranging at low gains. Ranging = take profits faster
Reduce fraction in trending at low gains. Trending = hold more position
Tradier-specific: which TFs signal WT exit for stocks. Currently 1h+4h+D. Stocks may need different than crypto
Tradier-specific: how many TFs must agree for stock exit. 1 = very sensitive. 3 = ride the wave until all turn
Tradier: use velocity vs cross for exit trigger. Currently False (cross only). Velocity might catch turns earlier
DC daytrade profit target. 1% current. Lower = more wins but smaller. Higher = fewer wins but bigger
DC daytrade stop loss. Note: this is the ONLY permitted % stop (daytrade-specific). Ratio to target matters most
Max hold time for DC daytrades. 240 = 4h. Shorter = cut losers. Longer = give more room
Min % outside DC channel for daytrade entry. Too small = false breaks. Too large = miss entries
Require 1h DC expanding for daytrade. Ensures higher-TF trend supports the breakout direction
Stoch K above this blocks long daytrade entry (chasing). Lower = stricter filter
Stoch K below this blocks short daytrade entry (chasing). Higher = stricter filter
Tradier: stoch cross on 1h triggers exit. Simple but effective mean-reversion exit signal
Tradier: MFI above this on 1h exits longs (overbought flow). Lower = earlier exit. Higher = ride longer
Tradier: MFI below this on 1h exits shorts (oversold flow). Higher = earlier exit
Tradier: enable MFI-based exits. MFI measures buying/selling pressure. Exhausted flow = exit
Stoch K must drop below this before long reentry allowed. Prevents chasing. Lower = stricter pullback required
Stoch K must rise above this before short reentry. Higher = stricter bounce required
Tradier: use cross-TF WT composite scoring. Aggregates all TFs into single score. Could be noise or signal
Reentry at better price: size multiplier vs original. 1.5 = 50% bigger (rewarding patience)
Reentry at worse price: size multiplier. 0.8 = 20% smaller (penalizing bad timing)
Max minutes before forced Tier 2 reentry. Prevents being out of position too long
Hard cap on DC width multiplier. Safety valve against extreme volatility over-sizing
dc_position_1h above this for LONG = near top of 1h channel = end of move. Exit signal.
dc_position_4h above this for LONG = 4h channel top. Slower but stronger exit signal.
dc_position_D above this for LONG = daily channel top. Strongest exit signal — end of multi-day move.
dc_position_15m below this = bottom of 15m channel = entry zone for longs.
dc_position_1h below this for long entry. 1h gives better signal than 15m (less noise).
dc_position_4h below this for long entry. 4h = slow mean-reversion setup.
dc_position_D below this for long entry. Daily = strongest mean-reversion but rare.
Exit when 1h dc_width contracts (channel narrowing = momentum dying). Use dc_width_1h < dc_width_1h_prev.
Exit when 4h dc_width contracts. Slower signal — confirms 1h contraction.
Minimum dc_width_1h for entry. Too narrow = no trend = no trade. Filters sideways chop.
Exit LONG when price crosses below dc_basis (channel midpoint). Midpoint loss = trend dying.
Exit SHORT when price crosses above dc_basis. Mirror of above.
Enter LONG on dc_high4 breakout (4-bar fast channel). Momentum confirmation.
Enter SHORT on dc_low4 breakdown. Mirror of above.
Use weighted sum of dc_position across TFs (5m:1 15m:2 1h:3 4h:4 D:5) for entry scoring.
Weight of 5m dc_position in combined DC score. 0=ignore 5m.
Weight of 15m dc_position in combined DC score.
Weight of 1h dc_position in combined DC score. Higher = 1h matters more.
Weight of 4h dc_position in combined DC score.
Weight of D dc_position in combined DC score. Highest weight = daily channel is king.
